title: 2025 HKDSE · Sea Friends

source.title: HKDSE English Language 2025 Paper 3 Part A — Task 1
source.notes: 来自你已有的 2025 真题录音、题目、逐字稿和评分参考。本练习截取完整 Task 1 访谈，未包含整卷广播说明与音乐；练习中的复听和字幕与正式考试一次播放的安排不同。题目见 Part A 第 4–5 页，逐字稿见 PDF 第 2 页，评分参考见 PDF 第 6 页。 字幕已对照原稿校正；24 个词暂只按整句定位。
source.timingMethod: acoustic word alignment with source-script comparison
source.timingReview: Source wording verified against tapescript; unresolved word times remain null.

instructions: Stella Poon and Adrian Timpson host a podcast about health and fitness in Hong Kong. They are now talking with a guest, Ricky Harrison, who is the founder of a charity called Sea Friends. Listen to the interview and complete the information in the spaces below. The first one has been provided as an example. You now have 30 seconds to study the task. At the end of the task, you will have one minute to tidy up your answers.
example: When Ricky started Sea Friends: 10 years ago.

questions.prompt: The number of people who have learned to swim with Sea Friends: ___
questions.explanation: 这里问已学会游泳的人数。Ricky 说 About 7,000 so far，要把千位数字听准。

questions.prompt: How long it takes to learn how to swim with Sea Friends: ___
questions.explanation: 评分参考接受 a few months 或 20 hours。Stella 误听成 a few hours，Adrian 随即纠正：No, he said 20 hours。要跟到纠正后的信息。

questions.prompt: Who Sea Friends mainly helps: ___ and ___（填写两个群体）
answers: high school students and their parents
their parents and high school students
questions.explanation: 这题有两个空，要同时保留 high school students 和 their parents。只写学生或只写家长都少了一个信息点。
录音直接说 We meet on Sundays。原句说明这是学生和家长较有空的时间。

questions.prompt: Ricky first went swimming with his ___.
questions.explanation: 题目问第一次跟谁游泳，答案是 older sister。四岁、紫色徽章、七岁停止游泳是附近的信息，不是这个空所问的内容。

questions.prompt: He stopped swimming because his coach ___.
questions.explanation: 原因是教练总对他大喊。Ricky 在录音里说 at me；填到题目的第三人称句子时要改成 at him 或 at Ricky。

questions.prompt: He started swimming again because he wanted to ___.
answers: teach his own kids to swim
teach his own kids how to swim
teach his own children to swim
teach his own children how to swim
questions.explanation: 他说成为父亲后，想教自己的孩子游泳。题目已经有 wanted to，空内从 teach 开始；my own kids 改为 his own kids。
要听新教练的身份。He was an old school friend, actually，指以前的同学；不是之前对他大喊的教练。

questions.prompt: Next year's Sea Friends event — Name of event: ___
questions.explanation: 这里填活动名称 Grand Island Project。可以先记音，再用复听核对专名拼写。

questions.prompt: Next year's Sea Friends event — Details of event: ___
answers: to swim around every island in Hong Kong
swim around every island in Hong Kong
swimming around every island in Hong Kong
questions.explanation: 要交代做什么和范围：swim around every island in Hong Kong。保留 around、every island 和 Hong Kong；只填岛屿数量或活动名称不够。

questions.prompt: Three reasons why Ricky recommends joining Sea Friends — reason 1: ___
answers: members do not need to pay
members don't need to pay anything
members do not need to pay anything
swimming's the best kind of exercise
swimming is the best kind of exercise
there is nothing better than swimming
questions.explanation: 第 11–13 题可以任意顺序填写三个不同理由：免费；游泳是最好的运动；认识不同的人或交朋友。同一个理由重复填写只计一次。

intro: 听 Stella、Adrian 访问 Sea Friends 创办人 Ricky，完成第 1–13 题。首听提交后再开启字幕与答案证据。

sentences.speaker: Stella
sentences.text: Hello, everyone.

sentences.speaker: Stella
sentences.text: Today, we're continuing our mission to find out what people in Hong Kong are doing to become fitter and more active.

sentences.speaker: Adrian
sentences.text: We sure are and we've got with us Ricky Harrison, the founder of Sea Friends, a charity which provides swimming lessons and organises swimming events here in Hong Kong.

sentences.speaker: Adrian
sentences.text: Ricky, can you tell us about that?

sentences.speaker: Adrian
sentences.text: When did you start Sea Friends?

sentences.speaker: Ricky
sentences.text: Well, that was in the summer of 2015, so ten years ago.

sentences.speaker: Stella
sentences.text: Ten years already!

sentences.speaker: Stella
sentences.text: And how many people have learned to swim with you?

sentences.speaker: Ricky
sentences.text: About 7,000 so far.

sentences.speaker: Stella
sentences.text: That's amazing.

sentences.speaker: Stella
sentences.text: How long does it take for someone to learn how to swim with you?

sentences.speaker: Ricky
sentences.text: Well, with regular lessons, most people manage it in a few months.

sentences.speaker: Ricky
sentences.text: I'd guess that most of our learners need about 20 hours.

sentences.speaker: Stella
sentences.text: Wow.

sentences.speaker: Stella
sentences.text: Only a few hours?

sentences.speaker: Adrian
sentences.text: No, he said 20 hours.

sentences.speaker: Adrian
sentences.text: That's a few months.

sentences.speaker: Adrian
sentences.text: But, Ricky, who are these learner swimmers?

sentences.speaker: Adrian
sentences.text: Who does Sea Friends help?

sentences.speaker: Ricky
sentences.text: At the moment, most of our members are high school students.

sentences.speaker: Ricky
sentences.text: Oh, and their parents.

sentences.speaker: Ricky
sentences.text: We have a lot of parents taking part.

sentences.speaker: Adrian
sentences.text: And when do the Sea Friends members meet?

sentences.speaker: Ricky
sentences.text: We meet on Sundays because that's when the students tend to be free.

sentences.speaker: Adrian
sentences.text: And the parents, of course.

sentences.speaker: Ricky
sentences.text: Sure, the parents too.

sentences.speaker: Stella
sentences.text: Ricky, tell us a bit about yourself as a swimmer.

sentences.speaker: Ricky
sentences.text: OK, well... I started swimming when I was four, with my older sister, and I remember getting my first award.

sentences.speaker: Ricky
sentences.text: It was a purple badge, and I was so proud.

sentences.speaker: Ricky
sentences.text: But when I was seven, I stopped swimming.

sentences.speaker: Adrian
sentences.text: Oh?

sentences.speaker: Adrian
sentences.text: Why was that?

sentences.speaker: Ricky
sentences.text: Because of my swimming coach.

sentences.speaker: Ricky
sentences.text: She was a good swimmer, but she was always shouting at me.

sentences.speaker: Adrian
sentences.text: Hmm... that can't have been pleasant.

sentences.speaker: Adrian
sentences.text: But you took up swimming again later.

sentences.speaker: Adrian
sentences.text: Why did you decide to start swimming again?

sentences.speaker: Ricky
sentences.text: Simple: I became a dad and I wanted to teach my own kids to swim.

sentences.speaker: Adrian
sentences.text: Ah, swimming together as a family is great, isn't it?

sentences.speaker: Ricky
sentences.text: It really is, but then I thought if I was going to be a teacher, I should get better at swimming myself so I looked for a new coach, and I found one.

sentences.speaker: Ricky
sentences.text: He was an old school friend, actually.

sentences.speaker: Stella
sentences.text: What has Sea Friends got planned for the future, Ricky?

sentences.speaker: Stella
sentences.text: Anything on the horizon?

sentences.speaker: Ricky
sentences.text: I'm glad you asked.

sentences.speaker: Ricky
sentences.text: Next year we're starting the Grand Island Project.

sentences.speaker: Ricky
sentences.text: We're all really excited about it.

sentences.speaker: Stella
sentences.text: And what's the Grand Island Project?

sentences.speaker: Ricky
sentences.text: We're going to swim around every island in Hong Kong.

sentences.speaker: Adrian
sentences.text: That must be 250 islands.

sentences.speaker: Adrian
sentences.text: How are you going to manage that?

sentences.speaker: Ricky
sentences.text: 263 islands to be precise.

sentences.speaker: Ricky
sentences.text: We're not doing all the islands at once, but we will eventually swim around every island in Hong Kong.

sentences.speaker: Ricky
sentences.text: It's going to take a while, but it's a group effort and teams can choose which island they want to do.

sentences.speaker: Adrian
sentences.text: Sounds "Grand" indeed.

sentences.speaker: Adrian
sentences.text: Good luck with it.

sentences.speaker: Stella
sentences.text: Ricky, you told us before we recorded that Sea Friends is opening up for anyone to join.

sentences.speaker: Stella
sentences.text: So, why should our listeners join Sea Friends?

sentences.speaker: Ricky
sentences.text: Well, it's free for one thing.

sentences.speaker: Ricky
sentences.text: Members don't need to pay anything.

sentences.speaker: Ricky
sentences.text: And there's nothing better than swimming.

sentences.speaker: Ricky
sentences.text: Swimming is the best kind of exercise.

sentences.speaker: Ricky
sentences.text: I tell this to everybody.

sentences.speaker: Ricky
sentences.text: Another reason to join is you meet so many different people.

sentences.speaker: Ricky
sentences.text: That's my favourite part: all the friends you make.

sentences.speaker: Stella
sentences.text: You heard it here first, listeners.

sentences.speaker: Stella
sentences.text: If you want to meet people and get the best kind of exercise, join Sea Friends.

sentences.speaker: Stella
sentences.text: Thanks for joining us, Ricky.

sentences.speaker: Ricky
sentences.text: You're welcome.
